StackType.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 25.) The 15 `on_stack` no-op overrides are DELETED; the base `Power.on_stack` adds, matching PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236), which adds unconditionally with no StackType branch -- PowerStackType.Single means 'Amount is hidden and displayed as 1' (PowerStackType.cs:10-13), not 'does not stack'. All 16 units re-verified against their own C#: 15 are StackType.Single, and NONE overrides InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144 default None), so none needs T1's instance machinery instead of amount-adding. Two per-site exceptions, both verified: (1) DAMPEN's C# StackType is actually `None`, not Single (DampenPower.cs:22) -- the queue's 16-unit list was wrong about it; its only applier, MagiKnight, dedupes caller-side (MagiKnight.cs:78-96: re-application calls AddCaster only and never reaches PowerCmd.Apply), so the deletion is inert through the real caller and T28's caster-set machinery is untouched and re-pinned. (2) HEX genuinely reads Amount (HexPower.cs:79 feeds CardCmd.Afflict<Hexed>(card, Amount)), so this deletion closes a real divergence that remains DORMANT only because SpectralKnight's move machine never loops back to HEX and KnightsElite fields exactly one -- a second Hex applier makes it live. ILLUSION needed no override and is unchanged (the opposite-sign case the record notes). No reachable re-application among the other 13: Burrowed and Soar re-apply only after their own expire/remove, always onto a fresh instance. Pins: test/test_stack_type_single.py (39 tests).  The text it replaced read: PowerStackType.None (DampenPower.cs:22) with the sim's on_stack overridden to `pass` citing it -- the census's wrong-reasoning class (`py audit/tools/power_census.py stack`, which lists this unit as the single StackType=None member). PowerCmd.ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:236) adds unconditionally regardless of StackType, so a second application really does reach Amount 2 in C#. DORMANT: nothing on either side reads Dampen's Amount (the downgrade is one level per card and the restore is per-card bookkeeping), and monsters/glory/knights.py:71-72 applies it with amount 1. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterApplied.issue: Two findings. (1) MECHANISM, the same substitution as illusion's: C#'s AfterApplied runs after PowerCmd registers the power; the sim does the work in __init__, i.e. inside `power_cls(...)` at cmds.py:324 and therefore BEFORE hooks.register and hooks.on_power_applied. Unobservable today (nothing reacts to a Dampen application) but it is the mechanism note the main report's section 7 item 6 asks for. (2) `all_cards` vs `AllCards` -- the NEW bug class: C# sweeps `base.Owner.Player.PlayerCombatState.AllCards.Where(c => c.IsUpgraded)` (DampenPower.cs:31), which is Hand+Draw+Discard+Exhaust+**Play** (PlayerCombatState.cs:70-80), where the sim's `owner.all_cards` (player.py:100-103) omits Play. DORMANT: Dampen is applied by the Magi Knight's move during the ENEMY turn (monsters/glory/knights.py:71-72), and the sim's Play limbo is only occupied between combat.py:433 (`hand.remove(card)`) and combat.py:498 (`_playing_card = None`), i.e. inside a player card play -- so no card can be in Play when this fires. Trigger: any Dampen application from a player-turn source. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: C# tracks a SET of casters (`Data.casters`, added through the public non-override `AddCaster`, DampenPower.cs:15/73-76) and removes the power only when the LAST caster dies (`casters.Remove(creature); if (casters.Count == 0) PowerCmd.Remove(this)`, DampenPower.cs:47-55). The sim keeps a single `self.applier` and expires on that one creature's death (powers.py:3176-3179). With two Magi Knights the game would keep the downgrade until both are dead and the sim would restore the upgrades on the first death. DORMANT, by enumeration rather than assertion: KNIGHTS_ELITE is `monster_classes=[FlailKnight, SpectralKnight, MagiKnight]` (monsters/glory/knights.py:129-131) -- exactly ONE Magi Knight -- and no other ported content applies Dampen (`grep DampenPower` outside powers.py finds only knights.py:71-72). Trigger: a second Dampen applier in one combat. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterRemoved.rationale: C# restores `num` upgrade levels per card where `num` is the level recorded at downgrade time (DampenPower.cs:60-69); the sim restores with `while card.upgrade_level < level: card.upgrade()` (powers.py:3182-3184). Those agree only because C#'s CardCmd.Downgrade is a FULL reset -- CardCmd.cs:221 -> CardModel.DowngradeInternal (CardModel.cs:2135-2148) sets `CurrentUpgradeLevel = 0` and re-clones the canonical DynamicVars -- so re-applying `num` upgrades lands exactly on `num`. The sim's `card.downgrade()` (cards/base.py:150-165) drops ONE level and its docstring claims it "Mirrors CardCmd.Downgrade", which is wrong in wording; it is right in EFFECT, and that was checked rather than assumed: **no card in the game has MaxUpgradeLevel > 1.** `grep -rn 'override int MaxUpgradeLevel' src/Core/Models/Cards/` returns only overrides to 0 plus Mocks/MockCardModel.cs, and `grep -rn 'max_upgrade_level = [2-9]' sts2_rl/` returns nothing -- so upgrade_level is always 0 or 1 and drop-one == drop-to-zero. Faithful, with the wording flagged for the card stream. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `wasRemovalPrevented: true` is passed when Hook.ShouldDie returned FALSE, i.e. when the DEATH was prevented (CreatureCmd.cs:566), and `false` on the real-death path (CreatureCmd.cs:519) -- the parameter is misnamed in the decompiled source and is NOT about ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath (computed separately at CreatureCmd.cs:508). So `!wasRemovalPrevented` means "the creature actually died". The sim fires hooks.on_death ONLY on the should_die-returned-True branch (cmds.py:98-105) and fires nothing on the prevented branch, so the guard is satisfied structurally. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.what: DampenPower.cs:34 `downgradedCardsToOldUpgradeLevels.Add(item, ...)` -- Dictionary.Add throws on a duplicate key
guards.rationale: The sim guards with `if card.upgrade_level > 0 and card not in self._downgraded` (powers.py:3169). C# is protected by AfterApplied firing once per new power; the sim's extra test is defensive and cannot change the outcome.

guards.issue: A public non-override method, so the harness does not enumerate it -- recorded so a reader does not think it was skipped (the same courtesy the main report gives CrueltyPower.ModifyVulnerableMultiplier). It is the writer of the `casters` set the AfterDeath entry is about, and the sim has no analogue: the sim's applier is set once by PowerCmd.apply (cmds.py:324) and never added to. DORMANT, same mechanism and same reachability as the AfterDeath entry above (both are the same multi-caster-tracking gap, read at two different lines of DampenPower.cs): AddCaster is only ever CALLED a second time when a second Dampen applier joins an existing Dampen on the same owner, and no such second caster exists in ported content. EXECUTED: `grep -rn DampenPower sts2_rl/*.py sts2_rl/**/*.py` (excluding powers.py itself) finds exactly one applier, `monsters/glory/knights.py:72` (`PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, DampenPower, 1, applier=self)`), inside `MagiKnight._dampen` (or equivalent move method); and `grep -n MagiKnight sts2_rl/monsters/**/*.py` shows the class is referenced in exactly one Encounter, `KNIGHTS_ELITE` (knights.py:133-136, `monster_classes=[FlailKnight, SpectralKnight, MagiKnight]` -- ONE MagiKnight instance per encounter, and no other encounter definition anywhere in sts2_rl/monsters includes it. Trigger: a second Dampen applier reaching the same owner in one combat -- e.g. two Magi Knights, or a second ported monster/relic/card that grants DampenPower.
